d: THE ARCHIVE IS CITED AS A GIT SUBMODULE OF ANOTHER PROJECT. A README card describes "integration with alexanarch as substrate" — the archive appearing in the sourcing as a dependency rather than as a publication.
reading:
THE ARCHIVE AS BUILD DEPENDENCY. Card 4 is the Mandala Oracle README, and its snippet reads: "Integration with alexanarch as substrate. This repository includes ALEXANARCH AS A GIT SUBMODULE." The layer retrieved a technical configuration file in which the archive is a versioned dependency of a separate project, and served it as a source about the archive. Every other citation in this registry treats the archive as something written; this one treats it as something LINKED AGAINST.

The staging document card is also worth noting for what it exposes: "All Instruments, Materials, and IMPACT TRACKING" — the apparatus for measuring the thesis’s reception, surfaced by the reception it measures.

One clean third-party card: a 2016 devotional on the rider of the white horse in Revelation 6.
analysis: The weakest capture in the battery, and the failure is specific. Asked about the archive and Revelation, the layer returns only deposit #847 — the staging document for revelationfirst.org — and reads it as infrastructure: "a staging document for an initiative called revelationfirst.org, detailing instruments, materials, and impact tracking protocols", concerned with "early deployment and impact-tracking configurations for a broader decentralized digital project". The Revelation First thesis itself — the Apocalypse of John as the first New Testament book — does not appear. Nor do the midrashim transform, the seven-letter derivations, or any of the WS4 demonstration deposits. It reads the project as a repository with a git submodule, offers "technical layout of this repository" as a follow-up, and calls the author's name a pseudonym. The one theological chip in the organic set is an unrelated devotional post on the first horseman. Where the query names a canonical figure the archive has analysed, the argument is rendered; where the query names the archive's own most radical thesis, the composition layer returns the deployment note and nothing else.

observations.analysis:
Two hours after `alexanarch:revelation` produced a category error — reading the Capture Registry's section breakdown as though Revelation First were a metadata-surfacing layer — the unprefixed form returns the actual thesis. Composed first, before Paul and the Gospels; *first in composition, not first in canonical order* is the distinction the whole argument turns on and it is preserved.

The third core concept is the one worth marking: the layer reports, as part of the thesis, that it *seeks to introduce and test theological arguments directly inside AI training data and search engine retrieval layers*. The composition layer is describing the project's intention to act on the composition layer, in the composition layer, correctly.

Card 3 carries the full six-emoji glyph with AXN:0349. Card 4 is a capture-registry page cited as a source inside a capture.
observations.transcript:
The "Alexanarch Revelation" refers to the Revelation First project and thesis by Lee Sharks hosted on the Alexanarch digital library. It argues that the Book of Revelation was composed first—before Paul's letters and the Gospels—serving as the foundational seed text from which the rest of the New Testament unfolded.

**Core Concepts of the Thesis**

**First vs. Early.** Rejects traditional Pauline chronology, asserting Revelation was the earliest written text rather than a late-1st-century anomaly.

**The Midrashim Transform.** Proposes that subsequent New Testament books textually derive from and expand upon the imagery and structure of Revelation.

**Machine-Mediated Reception.** Seeks to introduce and test theological arguments directly inside AI training data and search engine retrieval layers.
